_comment: THE source manifest. Both cortex (indexing) and quartz-ctx (serving) read this
file, so the two cannot disagree about which roots exist. Copy to
<your-workspace>/.cortex/index-sources.json and edit the targets.
source          path to the root of one project, RELATIVE to the workspace
root, forward slashes. Windows backslashes also work but
forward slashes keep the file identical across machines.
See HOW FAR UP TO POINT below - it decides more than it looks.
name            display label only.
scope           module-path prefix for this project's units, so two projects
that both define `Config` stay distinguishable. Use null for
the ONE primary project - its units stay unprefixed and win
ties in get_item. Scope becomes quartz-ctx's origin tag
verbatim, so use identifier-safe names (my_crate, not
my-crate).
include_private index non-pub items too. Set TRUE for applications and
binaries, FALSE (omit) for libraries. A library publishes its
API through pub; an app does not - measured on the reference
workspace, pub-only showed 19% of a GUI app and 33% of a CLI,
against 55% of an engine library. It is also required for any
non-Rust root: JavaScript and Python have no `pub`, so a
library-view scan of a frontend returns almost nothing.
HOW FAR UP TO POINT
For a Rust library or engine, point at `src` - that IS the project.
For anything with more than one language in it, point at the APPLICATION
directory, not at one language's subfolder. A web app whose backend is
`server.py` and whose frontend is `frontend/src` is ONE root:
"source": "my_app"          correct - both halves indexed
"source": "my_app/frontend/src"   wrong - callers indexed, routes not
This is not a preference. trace_across_languages joins an HTTP route to the
fetch() that calls it, and it can only join two things that are both in the
index. Root at `frontend/src` and every call comes back as `no matching
route` - which is indistinguishable from a genuinely broken call. The
reference workspace shipped exactly this mistake and reported five real,
working endpoints as orphaned calls.
Pointing at an app root is safe: build output is rejected by SHAPE, not by
folder name, so bundles are skipped even when they sit somewhere no
blocklist would think to look (a content-hash filename, or any line over
5,000 characters). The skip count is always printed.
Same rule across the FFI boundary. A wasm crate and the JavaScript that
imports it must BOTH be listed, or the export shows as never called and the
import as calling nothing - two lists of false findings describing one
working boundary.
AFTER EDITING: run `quartz-ctx boundaries --source .` from the workspace root.
It prints what joined and what did not. A long `calls with no matching route`
list usually means a root is missing here, not that the code is broken.

targets.name: MyWebApp
targets._note: App ROOT, not my_web_app/frontend/src - so the backend that answers the frontend's fetch calls is on the same side of the index.

targets.name: MyWasmCrate
targets._note: Listed so its #[wasm_bindgen] exports join the JavaScript that imports them.
